proof:
Source: Simon 7.3.3, proof of 3.3(1), display (12) (book/chapter-07.txt lines 478–482: "by using the compactness theorem 2.4 together with the monotonicity 4.7 of Ch. 4, one readily checks that if S_i ⇀ S … and if y, y_i ∈ B_1(0) with lim y_i = y, then Θⁿ(S, y) ≥ lim sup Θⁿ(S_i, y_i)"), in its threshold form, with the existence of Θⁿ from the monotonicity formula as in the proof of 7.3.1(1) (chapter-07.txt lines 326–328: "we can apply the monotonicity formula of 4.7 of Ch. 4 … to deduce that Θⁿ(T, x) exists for every x ∈ U and is an upper semi-continuous function of x"). The book omits the details ("one readily checks"); they are those of the parent proof, Step 0 (Lemma D = parent step 4, "Semicontinuity along members") combined with step 5 ("Densities exist on B_2(0)"), stated directly for the density Θ = dens so that the parent can apply it in step 6 (constant sequence μ_j = μ) and in step 7 (A.3)(3) (a subsequence of measures of the class). The vague-limit claim of parent step D3 (limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) for compact K) is supplied by the sibling vague_portmanteau (Submission.cbr_vague_portmanteau) with U = ℝ^P. Two details differ from the printed Lemma D, without changing its content: the existence of the densities (hypotheses of Lemma D) is proved inside, in Step 2 below, from (M) exactly as in parent step 5; and the passage from the closed balls B̄_{ρ+η}(w) back to open balls (parent D3–D4, η ↓ 0 and ρ = t/(1 + ε)) is done by the left-continuity argument of Step 7, using B̄_{ρ+η}(w) ⊆ B_t(w) for ρ + η < t.
Notation. ω := unitBallVolume n = volume(B_1(0) ⊆ Euclid n) ∈ [0, ∞]. For a measure ν, x ∈ ℝ^P and ρ ∈ ℝ: q(ν, x, ρ) := ν(B_ρ(x))/(ω·ofReal(ρⁿ)) and Θ(ν, x) := (limsup_{ρ→0⁺} q(ν, x, ρ)).toReal, as in the statement. All limits ρ → 0⁺ are along 𝓝[>]0, a nontrivial filter.
1. (Constants.) ω is the Haar volume of the nonempty, open, bounded unit ball of Euclid n, so 0 < ω < ∞ (measure_ball_pos for the open-positive measure volume; measure_ball_lt_top in the proper space Euclid n); this includes n = 0. For ρ > 0, ρⁿ > 0, so ω·ofReal(ρⁿ) ∈ (0, ∞), and ofReal(e^{Λρ}/ρⁿ)·ofReal(ρⁿe^{−Λρ}) = ofReal(e^{Λρ}·e^{−Λρ}) = ofReal(1) = 1 (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, both reals nonnegative).
2. (Monotone density lemma.) Let ν be a measure on ℝ^P that is finite on compact sets, x ∈ ℝ^P and R > 0, and suppose g(ρ) := ofReal(e^{Λρ}/ρⁿ)·ν(B_ρ(x)) is nondecreasing on (0, R). Then (i) q(ν, x, ρ) → ofReal(Θ(ν, x)) as ρ → 0⁺, and (ii) ω·ofReal(Θ(ν, x))·ofReal(ρⁿe^{−Λρ}) ≤ ν(B_ρ(x)) for every ρ ∈ (0, R).
 Proof. (a) [0, ∞] is a complete linear order and g is nondecreasing on the nonempty interval (0, R), so g(ρ) → L := inf{g(ρ) : 0 < ρ < R} as ρ → 0⁺ (MonotoneOn.tendsto_nhdsWithin_Ioo_right; g is bounded below by 0). L ≤ g(R/2) = ofReal(e^{ΛR/2}/(R/2)ⁿ)·ν(B_{R/2}(x)) ≤ ofReal(…)·ν(B̄_{R/2}(x)) < ∞, because the closed ball is compact. (b) For ρ > 0, q(ν, x, ρ) = (ofReal(e^{−Λρ})/ω)·g(ρ): indeed ofReal(e^{−Λρ})·ofReal(e^{Λρ}/ρⁿ) = ofReal((ρⁿ)⁻¹) = ofReal(ρⁿ)⁻¹ (ENNReal.ofReal_inv_of_pos), and (ω·ofReal(ρⁿ))⁻¹ = ω⁻¹·ofReal(ρⁿ)⁻¹ (ENNReal.mul_inv, both factors in (0, ∞)), so both sides equal ν(B_ρ(x))·ω⁻¹·ofReal(ρⁿ)⁻¹. (c) ρ ↦ ofReal(e^{−Λρ}) is continuous with value 1 at 0, and division by the constant ω ≠ 0 is continuous, so ofReal(e^{−Λρ})/ω → ω⁻¹ as ρ → 0⁺. Since ω⁻¹ < ∞ and L < ∞, the product rule for limits in [0, ∞] (ENNReal.Tendsto.mul) and (b) give q(ν, x, ρ) → ω⁻¹·L as ρ → 0⁺. Hence limsup_{ρ→0⁺} q(ν, x, ρ) = ω⁻¹·L < ∞ (Tendsto.limsup_eq), so ofReal(Θ(ν, x)) = ofReal((ω⁻¹L).toReal) = ω⁻¹·L, which proves (i). (d) For ρ ∈ (0, R), L ≤ g(ρ). Hence ω·ofReal(Θ(ν, x))·ofReal(ρⁿe^{−Λρ}) = ω·ω⁻¹·L·ofReal(ρⁿe^{−Λρ}) = L·ofReal(ρⁿe^{−Λρ}) ≤ g(ρ)·ofReal(ρⁿe^{−Λρ}) = ν(B_ρ(x))·[ofReal(e^{Λρ}/ρⁿ)·ofReal(ρⁿe^{−Λρ})] = ν(B_ρ(x)), by ω·ω⁻¹ = 1 (0 < ω < ∞) and step 1. This proves (ii).
3. (Trivial case.) If c ≤ 0, then c ≤ 0 ≤ Θ(μ, w) because toReal is nonnegative. From now on c > 0.
4. (Radii.) Put r := (2 − |w|)/4 > 0. (α) If |w_j − w| < r, then B̄_{2r}(w_j) ⊆ B̄_2(0): for |z − w_j| ≤ 2r, |z| ≤ |z − w_j| + |w_j − w| + |w| < 2r + r + |w| ≤ 4r + |w| = 2. (β) B̄_{4r}(w) ⊆ B̄_2(0): for |z − w| ≤ 4r, |z| ≤ 4r + |w| = 2. (γ) Since w_j → w, for every η > 0 we have |w_j − w| < η for all sufficiently large j.
5. (Lower bounds for μ_j.) Let j satisfy |w_j − w| < r. By (M) for ν = μ_j at centre w_j and radius 2r (admissible by 4(α)), and finiteness of μ_j on compact sets, step 2(ii) gives ω·ofReal(Θ(μ_j, w_j))·ofReal(ρⁿe^{−Λρ}) ≤ μ_j(B_ρ(w_j)) for every ρ ∈ (0, 2r). Since c ≤ Θ(μ_j, w_j), ofReal(c) ≤ ofReal(Θ(μ_j, w_j)). With h(ρ) := ω·ofReal(c)·ofReal(ρⁿe^{−Λρ}) we get: h(ρ) ≤ μ_j(B_ρ(w_j)) whenever |w_j − w| < r and 0 < ρ < 2r.
6. (Vague limit.) Apply the sibling vague_portmanteau with U := ℝ^P (open), ν_j := μ_j and μ: its finiteness hypotheses (μ_j(K) < ∞ and μ(K) < ∞ for compact K) hold because all these measures are finite on compact sets, and its convergence hypothesis is (V) (the condition tsupport f ⊆ ℝ^P is automatic). Its first conclusion gives limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P.
7. (Transfer of the lower bound.) Fix t ∈ (0, 2r). (a) Let ρ ∈ (0, t), put η := (t − ρ)/2 > 0 and K := B̄_{ρ+η}(w), a compact set. By 4(γ), for all large j we have |w_j − w| < min(r, η); for such j, B_ρ(w_j) ⊆ K (|z − w| ≤ |z − w_j| + |w_j − w| < ρ + η), and ρ < t < 2r, so step 5 gives h(ρ) ≤ μ_j(B_ρ(w_j)) ≤ μ_j(K). As this holds for all large j, h(ρ) ≤ limsup_j μ_j(K) (le_limsup_of_frequently_le), and step 6 gives h(ρ) ≤ μ(K). Since ρ + η < t, K ⊆ B_t(w) (closedBall_subset_ball), so h(ρ) ≤ μ(B_t(w)) for every ρ ∈ (0, t). (b) h : ℝ → [0, ∞] is continuous: ρ ↦ ρⁿe^{−Λρ} is continuous, ofReal is continuous, and multiplication by the finite constant ω·ofReal(c) is continuous on [0, ∞]. The interval (0, t) belongs to 𝓝[<]t (Ioo_mem_nhdsLT), so letting ρ → t⁻ in (a) gives h(t) ≤ μ(B_t(w)) (le_of_tendsto).
8. (Ratio bound.) Let t ∈ (0, 2r). Since tⁿ ≥ 0, ofReal(tⁿe^{−Λt}) = ofReal(tⁿ)·ofReal(e^{−Λt}), so h(t) = [ofReal(c)·ofReal(e^{−Λt})]·[ω·ofReal(tⁿ)] with ω·ofReal(tⁿ) ∈ (0, ∞). By step 7, [ofReal(c)·ofReal(e^{−Λt})]·[ω·ofReal(tⁿ)] ≤ μ(B_t(w)), i.e. (ENNReal.le_div_iff_mul_le) ofReal(c)·ofReal(e^{−Λt}) ≤ μ(B_t(w))/(ω·ofReal(tⁿ)) = q(μ, w, t).
9. (Conclusion.) By (M) for ν = μ at centre w and radius 4r (admissible by 4(β)) and finiteness of μ on compact sets, step 2(i) gives q(μ, w, t) → ofReal(Θ(μ, w)) as t → 0⁺. By continuity, ofReal(c)·ofReal(e^{−Λt}) → ofReal(c)·ofReal(1) = ofReal(c) as t → 0⁺. The inequality of step 8 holds for every t ∈ (0, 2r), a set belonging to 𝓝[>]0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT), so le_of_tendsto_of_tendsto gives ofReal(c) ≤ ofReal(Θ(μ, w)). Since Θ(μ, w) ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff gives c ≤ Θ(μ, w). ∎
key_steps: Monotone density lemma: if ρ ↦ ofReal(e^{Λρ}/ρⁿ)ν(B_ρ(x)) is nondecreasing on (0, R) and ν is finite on compacts, the ratio q(ν, x, ·) tends to the finite value ofReal(Θ(ν, x)), and ω·ofReal(Θ(ν, x))·ofReal(ρⁿe^{−Λρ}) ≤ ν(B_ρ(x)) for ρ < R.
Trivial case c ≤ 0; otherwise with r = (2 − |w|)/4 the monotonicity hypothesis applies at w_j (radius 2r, |w_j − w| < r) and at w (radius 4r).
c ≤ Θ(μ_j, w_j) gives h(ρ) := ω·ofReal(c)·ofReal(ρⁿe^{−Λρ}) ≤ μ_j(B_ρ(w_j)) for large j and ρ < 2r.
vague_portmanteau (U = ℝ^P): limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K); with K = B̄_{ρ+η}(w) ⊆ B_t(w) this gives h(ρ) ≤ μ(B_t(w)) for ρ < t, and continuity of h gives h(t) ≤ μ(B_t(w)).
Dividing by ω·tⁿ: ofReal(c)·ofReal(e^{−Λt}) ≤ q(μ, w, t); letting t → 0⁺ with the monotone density lemma at w gives ofReal(c) ≤ ofReal(Θ(μ, w)), hence c ≤ Θ(μ, w).
